       apples-to-apples, or is the "before" case handicapped / the "after" case flattered?
  (Q2) REPRODUCIBILITY: can a third party regenerate these results from what is on disk
       and what is documented?

  - /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cpu/     the kernel source (arch/riscv/repack.cpp, arch/riscv/quants.c, ggml-cpu.c)
  - git history (branch q1_0-rvv-opt), git log/show/diff

A log line looks like:
  [roi] MUL_MAT #57 src0=blk.7.attn_v.weight [5120 x 1024] nrows=4
  [andesim] 1630251 cycles

HARD RULE - DO NOT RUN LONG SIMULATIONS. A single RTL leg can take up to 20 HOURS.
Never invoke the simulator, never run a full 'bash sweep.sh' sweep, never build the model.
You MAY run: reading files, grep/awk/sed, git commands, arithmetic (python3/awk),
and cheap re-derivation from logs already on disk (e.g. 'bash sweep.sh --md' which only
re-formats existing logs - check the script first to confirm it does not launch runs).

RULES OF EVIDENCE:
  - Every finding must cite the exact file/line/log/command that establishes it.
  - Quote the document's claim verbatim in claim_in_doc.
  - Report BOTH what checks out and what does not. An audit that only lists problems is
    as useless as one that only praises. Populate verified_ok generously.
  - Do not speculate. If you cannot verify something with the evidence at hand, mark it
    'unverifiable' and say precisely what evidence would be needed.
  - Severity: critical = a headline number is wrong or the comparison is rigged;
    major = a real methodological bias or a blocked reproduction;
    minor = imprecision that does not change a conclusion; info = an observation.


You are an ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER. Another auditor filed the finding below on
/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/profiling_gemm_27b.md. Your job is to try to REFUTE it. Default to refuted=true
if you cannot independently reproduce the auditor's evidence.

LENS FOR YOUR CHECK: EVIDENCE - re-run or re-derive the auditor's check yourself from the raw logs/source/scripts. Did they read the right file? Is the quote accurate? Is their arithmetic right? Did they miss context elsewhere in the repo that explains it away?

FINDING
title: There is no RISC-V vector twin of the 4x1 activation quantizer; GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF is not what makes prefill scalar
severity: major
kind: evidence-gap
doc claim: Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
auditor checked: `grep -rn ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1 ggml/` returns exactly four hits: the declaration (repack.h:208), the alias (arch-fallback.h:221), the call (repack.cpp:348) and the definition of the *_generic* name (repack.cpp:51). Read repack.cpp:342-352, repack.cpp:12 (`#include "arch-fallback.h"`), and arch-fallback.h:216-256 (the `#elif defined(__riscv)` block, reached because the preceding branches at lines 7/76/88/118/167 are GGML_CPU_GENERIC/arm/x86/ppc/loongarch). Confirmed with `git log -L 342,352:ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp` (commit 8734bdb7e).
auditor concludes: arch-fallback.h:221 unconditionally does `#define ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` on every RISC-V build - there is no zvfh guard on that alias, and no RISC-V implementation of the vector routine exists anywhere in the tree. After preprocessing, the scalar body at repack.cpp:51 IS `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1`, so both arms of the `#if defined(__riscv_zvfh) && defined(__riscv_v)` at repack.cpp:347-351 resolve to the same scalar function. Building with -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=ON would not give prefill a vector quantizer. The author's own opt_roadmap.md (F4d, line ~207) states this correctly - 'un-gated quantize_mat_t<1,Q8_0> from zvfh (generic 4x1 otherwise)' - and lists 'activation quantize RVV' as a remaining lever, i.e. as unwritten code.
claimed impact: No cycle number or speedup in either table changes - prefill genuinely does run a scalar quantizer, which is what the measurements reflect. What changes is the cause and the remedy: the document points a reader at a build flag ('the measurement build sets -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF'), implying the measurement handicapped itself and that flipping one CMake option recovers the loss. It does not. The real work is writing an RVV `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` for RISC-V, which is what the closing sentence ('Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win') actually implies. A third party auditing the build config would conclude the run was mis-configured and dismiss the result.

| variant | gemm `F` | gemm `T` | gemv `F` | gemv `T` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `baseline` | 398,003 | 80,915 | 13,379 | 133,082 |
| `prefetch` | 441,355 | 76,544 | 27,294 | 85,084 |
| `d4` | 489,581 | 23,036 | 39,491 | 21,638 |

`T` collapses 3.5x (gemm) and 6.2x (gemv) as the kernel improves; `F` stays put,
and stays an order of magnitude apart between the two paths. It is the shared
activation path, and the source says what it is. `forward_mul_mat` quantizes
activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`), and the routine it
picks depends on the token count:

- **4 tokens** (`ne11 - ne11 % 4 == 4`) take
  `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>`, which selects
  `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` -- a **pure scalar** loop
  (`repack.cpp:51`, its own comment says `// scalar`): per 32-column block, 128
  `fabsf` for the amax scan plus 128 `roundf` plus the de-interleave index
  arithmetic. Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
- **2 tokens** are not a multiple of 4, so they fall through to `from_float` =
  `quantize_row_q8_0`, which **is** RVV-vectorized on RISC-V
  (`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`).

So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the
whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap, and at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest
single item in a small prefill matmul -- bigger than the kernel it feeds.
Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win.
